recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中有一個核分六葉以上的嗜中性球（hypersegmented neutrophil），紅血球大小不均，混有大卵圓紅血球、淚滴細胞與破碎紅血球（schistocytes），血小板稀少；過度分葉的嗜中性球與大卵圓細胞提示維生素 B12 缺乏，而非 TTP。
features: Hypersegmented neutrophil with six or more nuclear lobes
Marked anisopoikilocytosis with macro-ovalocytes and a polychromatic macrocyte
Red cell fragments (schistocytes), teardrop cells and small dense microspherocyte-like fragments
No nucleated red cells or blasts in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (Wright-Giemsa) shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with macro-ovalocytes, teardrop cells and red cell fragments including schistocytes, along with a polychromatic macrocyte. A hypersegmented neutrophil with at least six nuclear lobes is present, and platelets appear decreased. The combination of schistocytes and thrombocytopenia can mimic a thrombotic microangiopathy, but the hypersegmented neutrophil and macro-ovalocytes indicate ineffective megaloblastic hematopoiesis. Findings are consistent with severe vitamin B12 deficiency causing pseudo-thrombotic microangiopathy; normal or near-normal ADAMTS13 activity, low reticulocytes and very high LDH support this diagnosis.

ddx.vs: TTP shows schistocytes with reticulocytosis and ADAMTS13 activity below 10%, without hypersegmented neutrophils or macro-ovalocytes.
Morphology is identical, so serum B12, folate, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels are needed to distinguish them.
MDS shows hypolobated or hypogranular neutrophils and dysplasia that does not correct with vitamin replacement.
HUS and DIC present with schistocytes plus renal failure or coagulopathy and lack megaloblastic features.
